findings.fix: Name Lung-RADS v2022 (ACR, November 2022) and bring the page to it (the differences are in the findings below); until then, a dated notice that v1.1 was replaced in November 2022. The v1.1 release year (2019) and publisher are right.
findings.question: Which should lead this page for readers in BC? (a) Lung-RADS v2022, by the audit rule (an ACR system; CAR has no lung screening guideline), with a short note on where the BC Cancer Lung Screening Program differs; or (b) the program's own BC Lung Screening Protocol v2.0 (January 2026), which program radiologists report program LDCTs with: PanCan nodule risk score at baseline, volumetry and volume doubling time at follow-up, categories 1–5 (1: back in 2 years; 2: 1 year; 3: repeat LDCT in 3 months; 4–5: the program arranges diagnostic referral), eligibility 55–74 with PLCOm2012 risk ≥ 1.5%, with Lung-RADS as the note? The BC standards never mention Lung-RADS. The page's "Application: Annual" screening also differs from the program's biennial category 1.

findings.piece: Calculator: new nodules (New = Yes)
findings.says: With "New nodule on this exam? Yes" the result depends on diameter alone, whatever the nodule type or solid component: runs gave < 4 mm → 3, 4 to < 6 mm → 4A, ≥ 6 mm → 4B. New solid 3.9 → 3 (expected 2), 4.0 and 5.9 → 4A (expected 3), 6.0 and 7.9 → 4B (expected 4A); new part-solid 5.9 mm total → 4A (expected 3), 10 mm with a 3.9 mm solid component → 4B (expected 4A); new ground glass 3.9 → 3, 10.0 and 29.9 → 4B (expected 2), 30.0 → 4B (expected 3).
findings.fix: Grade new nodules by type with the v2022 rows: solid < 4 → 2, 4–< 6 → 3, 6–< 8 → 4A, ≥ 8 → 4B; part-solid < 6 mm total → 3, new solid component < 4 → 4A, ≥ 4 → 4B; ground glass < 30 → 2, ≥ 30 → 3. Until then switch the calculator off: it raises every new nodule by a category, and a new 6–29 mm ground-glass nodule to 4B.

findings.question: Which leads for cystic renal masses? By the rule CAR 2019 leads (it gives the management, Flowchart 4 p. 128), but its Table 1 (p. 131) is the pre-2019 Bosniak classification: CAR searched the literature in March–June 2018 (p. 125) and Bosniak 2019 appeared in June 2019. Bosniak 2019 is endorsed by the Society of Abdominal Radiology, and the 2023 CUA guideline recommends it (Recommendation 2), though its authors say it "will need to be tested prior to widespread clinical implementation". Option A: Bosniak 2019 for the categories and CAR 2019 for management (the IIF schedule is the same in both; CAR adds ultrasound follow-up and urology referral for III/IV), with a short note where CAR's Table 1 differs. Option B: CAR 2019 throughout (pre-2019 classes), with Bosniak 2019 as the difference note. The classes differ on: enhancement (2019 has one definition and lets I/II walls and septa enhance; pre-2019 splits perceived/measurable and sends any measurable enhancement to III/IV); calcification (2019: any type is II; pre-2019: thick/nodular is IIF); hyperattenuating >3 cm (2019: II; pre-2019: IIF); IIF (2019: ≥4 thin or 3 mm enhancing septa/wall, plus heterogeneous T1 hyperintensity on MRI); III/IV (2019 puts ≤3 mm irregular thickening in III and defines a nodule by size and margin); and 2019 alone has MRI criteria and the attenuation-only class II types.

findings.piece: Ancillary features
findings.says: "LI-RADS v2018 allows upgrading or downgrading by one category based on ancillary features: Upgrade features (suggest HCC): Restricted diffusion, T1 hypointensity, T2 mild hyperintensity, transitional/hepatobiliary phase hypointensity, fat in mass. Downgrade features (suggest benign): Definite intralesional fat, blood products, intralesional gas, lesion stability ≥2 years"
findings.fix: Replace the lists with core p.9 (blood products and fat in mass favour HCC; gas and T1 hypointensity are not ancillary features) and add the rules: upgrade only up to LR-4, never to LR-5, and no adjustment when both kinds are present.

sources.citation: American College of Radiology. CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 core. 2018.
sources.location: p.9 (PDF p.12) Step 2: AFs are optional; ≥ 1 AF favoring malignancy upgrades by 1 category up to LR-4; ≥ 1 AF favoring benignity downgrades by 1; both present: do not adjust; AFs cannot be used to upgrade to LR-5. AFs favoring malignancy: US visibility, subthreshold growth, restricted diffusion, mild-moderate T2 hyperintensity, corona enhancement, fat sparing in solid mass, iron sparing in solid mass, TP hypointensity, HBP hypointensity; favoring HCC in particular: nonenhancing capsule, nodule-in-nodule, mosaic architecture, blood products in mass, fat in mass more than adjacent liver. AFs favoring benignity: size stability, size reduction, parallels blood pool, undistorted vessels, iron in mass more than liver, marked T2 hyperintensity, HBP isointensity; p.24-25 (PDF p.27-28) definitions ("Size stability ≥ 2 years")

findings.piece: Imaging protocol requirements
findings.says: "Adequate CT requires: unenhanced, late arterial, portal venous, and delayed phases. Adequate MRI requires: T2, DWI, unenhanced T1, late arterial, portal venous, delayed, and hepatobiliary phase (if hepatobiliary agent used)."
findings.fix: Use the core p.13 lists: unenhanced CT only after locoregional treatment; DWI suggested, not required; add T1 in- and opposed-phase; with gadoxetate the required late phases are transitional and hepatobiliary.

sources.citation: American College of Radiology. CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 core. 2018.
sources.location: p.13 (PDF p.16) Technical Recommendations: CT required: arterial (late arterial strongly preferred), portal venous and delayed phases, precontrast only if the patient has had locoregional treatment; MRI (ECA or gadobenate) required: unenhanced T1 out-of-phase and in-phase, T2, precontrast, arterial, portal venous and delayed phases, DWI suggested/optional; MRI gadoxetate required: T1 OP/IP, T2, precontrast, arterial, portal venous, transitional (2-5 min) and hepatobiliary phases, DWI suggested/optional
